walkthrough:
Evaluate the composite function $gg(x) = g(g(x))$:
$$gg(x) = g(2x - 3) = 2(2x - 3) - 3 = 4x - 6 - 3 = 4x - 9$$

Set $y = \frac{1}{x^2 - 9}$ and isolate $x$ for the domain $x > 3$:
$$x^2 - 9 = \frac{1}{y} \implies x^2 = \frac{1}{y} + 9 \implies x = \sqrt{\frac{1}{y} + 9}$$
$$f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{x} + 9}$$

Determine the domain of $f^{-1}$ from the range of $f$ for $x > 3$:
$$x > 3 \implies x^2 - 9 > 0 \implies f(x) > 0$$
$$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: \quad x > 0 \quad (\text{or } (0, \infty))$$

Form the composite function $fg(x) = f(g(x))$ and equate to $\frac{1}{7}$:
$$fg(x) = \frac{1}{(2x - 3)^2 - 9} = \frac{1}{7}$$

Equate the denominators and solve for $x$:
$$(2x - 3)^2 - 9 = 7 \implies (2x - 3)^2 = 16$$
$$2x - 3 = 4 \implies 2x = 7 \implies x = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5$$
$$2x - 3 = -4 \implies 2x = -1 \implies x = -\frac{1}{2} \quad (\text{rejected, as domain requires } x > 3)$$
$$x = \frac{7}{2}$$
